## 2.1 uv installs every dependency group {#step-02.1}

The tests need pytest, but the package does not. A person who installs wikiapp should not get pytest. So the tools
of the project go in dependency groups. A dependency group is a list of packages in `pyproject.toml` that the
project needs while we work on it. A user of the package never gets them. The test tools go in a group `test`, and
later the linters and the docs tools get groups of their own.

uv installs only the group `dev` by default. The setting `default-groups = "all"` makes `uv sync` and `uv run`
install every group. So each later `uv add --group` needs no other change to `pyproject.toml`. A patch adds the
table `[tool.uv]` with this setting.

[± See the change to `pyproject.toml`](#step-02.1-pyproject.toml-5d07e7-diff){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}

At the end of `pyproject.toml`, the new table `[tool.uv]` has the line `default-groups = "all"`, with a comment
above it.

The setting changes which groups uv installs, not which versions. So `uv.lock` still matches `pyproject.toml`.

```bash
uv lock --check
```

uv prints `Resolved 7 packages`, and no error. The project has no groups yet, so the setting changes nothing until a later move adds one.

### What changed {#step-02.1-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="step-02.1-pyproject.toml-5d07e7"></a>`pyproject.toml`: the table `[tool.uv]`, so uv installs every dependency group. 4 lines added. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/blob/46dc20fb9092170695699eaa052f4830563cb930/pyproject.toml){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}
  - look at `default-groups = "all"`

<a id="step-02.1-pyproject.toml-5d07e7-diff"></a>

<details><summary>The diff of <code>pyproject.toml</code></summary>

```diff
@@ -18,3 +18,7 @@ wikiapp = "wikiapp.console:main"
 [build-system]
 requires = ["uv_build>=0.12.13,<0.13.0"]
 build-backend = "uv_build"
+
+[tool.uv]
+# uv sync and uv run install every dependency group, not only dev
+default-groups = "all"
```

</details>

## 2.2 The first test {#step-02.2}

Nothing checks yet that the command works. The first test runs the command and checks that it ends with exit code
0. click's `CliRunner` runs a command in the same process as the test. It keeps the output and the exit code of
the command.

This test is an end-to-end test. It runs the whole command, and the command asks the real Wikipedia. So a failure
can come from the code, from the network or from Wikipedia.

The test comes in a new file, `tests/test_console.py`, as a patch. The patch also makes the folder `tests`.

[± See the new file `tests/test_console.py`](#step-02.2-tests-test_console.py-9442ee-diff){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}

The new file `tests/test_console.py` has one test, `test_main_succeeds`. It runs `console.main` with a
`CliRunner`, and checks `result.exit_code`.

pytest is not installed yet, so the test cannot run. `python -m pytest` uses the pytest of the project's `.venv`,
and never one from elsewhere.

```bash
uv run python -m pytest
```

The command fails on purpose. Python prints `No module named pytest`, and the exit code is 1. The next move installs pytest.

### What changed {#step-02.2-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="step-02.2-tests-test_console.py-9442ee"></a>`tests/test_console.py`: a test that runs the command and checks its exit code. New, 8 lines. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/blob/6d7a6cfdae6008a9687f3525348ab24ea05930cc/tests/test_console.py){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}
  - look at `assert result.exit_code == 0`

<a id="step-02.2-tests-test_console.py-9442ee-diff"></a>

<details><summary>The diff of <code>tests/test_console.py</code></summary>

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+import click.testing
+
+from wikiapp import console
+
+def test_main_succeeds():
+    runner = click.testing.CliRunner()
+    result = runner.invoke(console.main)
+    assert result.exit_code == 0
```

</details>

[This change on GitHub](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/commit/6d7a6cfdae6008a9687f3525348ab24ea05930cc){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary} [The code after it](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/tree/6d7a6cfdae6008a9687f3525348ab24ea05930cc){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary}

## 2.3 pytest, in the group test {#step-02.3}

The test needs pytest. `uv add --group test` writes pytest into a new group `test` of `pyproject.toml`, adds its
exact version to `uv.lock`, and installs it.

[pytest](https://docs.pytest.org/) is the test runner of most Python projects. It finds each function whose name
starts with `test_`, in the files whose names start with `test_`, and runs it. When an `assert` fails, it prints the
values on both sides.

This change came from running `uv add --group test pytest`.

At the end of `pyproject.toml`, the new table `[dependency-groups]` has the group `test`, with the line
`"pytest>=9.1.1",`. `uv.lock` has pytest 9.1.1, and iniconfig, packaging, pluggy and pygments, which pytest needs.
It also has colorama 0.4.6, which pytest needs on Windows.

```bash
uv run pytest
```

pytest finds `tests/test_console.py`, and prints `collected 1 item` and `1 passed`. The test asks the real
Wikipedia, so it needs the network.

### What changed {#step-02.3-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="step-02.3-pyproject.toml-5d07e7"></a>`pyproject.toml`: the group `test`, with pytest. 5 lines added. It comes from `uv add --group test pytest`. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/blob/d92e2dec921d6322e2a356af20dafef3837c1849/pyproject.toml){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}
  - look at `"pytest>=9.1.1",`
- <a id="step-02.3-uv.lock-8356d8"></a>`uv.lock`: pytest, and the packages that it needs. 69 lines added. It comes from `uv add --group test pytest`. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/blob/d92e2dec921d6322e2a356af20dafef3837c1849/uv.lock){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}

<a id="step-02.3-pyproject.toml-5d07e7-diff"></a>

<details><summary>The diff of <code>pyproject.toml</code></summary>

```diff
@@ -22,3 +22,8 @@ build-backend = "uv_build"
 [tool.uv]
 # uv sync and uv run install every dependency group, not only dev
 default-groups = "all"
+
+[dependency-groups]
+test = [
+    "pytest>=9.1.1",
+]
```

</details>

[This change on GitHub](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/commit/d92e2dec921d6322e2a356af20dafef3837c1849){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary} [The code after it](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/tree/d92e2dec921d6322e2a356af20dafef3837c1849){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary}

## 2.4 The recipe `just test` {#step-02.4}

The command that runs the tests is `uv run pytest`, with any options for pytest after it. A recipe `test` in the
justfile gives it a short name, `just test`. The words after `just test` go to pytest. `"$@"` stands for those
words, and the recipe gives each word to pytest whole. `just test help` shows the recipe.

[± See the change to `justfile`](#step-02.4-justfile-424f0b-diff){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}

At the end of the `justfile`, the recipe `test *args:` runs `uv run pytest "$@"`, or shows itself for
`just test help`. The comment above it is what `just` lists for the recipe.

`just` prints each line of a recipe before it runs the line, if the line does not start with `@`. So `just test`
prints `uv run pytest "$@"`, the command that it ran.

```bash
just --show test
just test
```

`just --show test` prints the comment and the recipe. `just test` prints `uv run pytest "$@"`, and then the same
result as before, `1 passed`.

### What changed {#step-02.4-what-changed-182c57}

- <a id="step-02.4-justfile-424f0b"></a>`justfile`: the recipe `test`. 6 lines added. [The file](https://github.com/rahuldave/smallwikiapp/blob/45807a0ddd9f97798c3f86a82b19782d4df45837/justfile){.btn .btn-sm .btn-secondary}
  - look at `test *args:`

<a id="step-02.4-justfile-424f0b-diff"></a>

<details><summary>The diff of <code>justfile</code></summary>

```diff
@@ -19,3 +19,9 @@ help *verb:
 [group('setup')]
 setup *args:
     @{{ if args == "help" { "just help setup" } else { "uv sync --locked" } }}
+
+# Run the tests. Extra arguments go to pytest: just test -k title
+[group('quality')]
+[no-exit-message]
+test *args:
+    {{ if args == "help" { "just help test" } else { 'uv run pytest "$@"' } }}
```

</details>
